title: Hairpin lace rectangular wrap
excerpt: A light rectangular wrap worked in sport weight yarn using a hairpin lace frame. The loops are joined down the centre with a simple joining row to hold the strips together.
sourceNotes: Three hairpin lace strips joined side by side to form a wide rectangular wrap, finished with a single crochet edging along the long edges.

glossaryTerms.definition: A U-shaped tool with two prongs that holds the working loops while the hook works a spine down the centre. The loop pairs build up on both prongs.
A method of connecting two hairpin lace strips by picking up loops from each side alternately with a crochet hook and working them together.

crochet.gaugeText: Each hairpin strip = 5 cm wide with prongs set 5 cm apart.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 45 cm wide x 130 cm long.

Set the frame to 5 cm. Slip loop onto left prong, chain 1. Work double crochet in centre, rotate frame, repeat until 200 loops sit on each side of the strip (400 loops total). Remove from frame carefully and secure the live loops with a stitch holder or length of scrap yarn.

Place two strips side by side. Pick up 1 loop from strip 1 and 1 loop from strip 2 onto the hook, chain through both. Continue alternating loops across the full length to join. Repeat to attach the third strip.
Work a row of double crochet along each long edge, spacing stitches evenly. Fasten off and weave in the ends with the tapestry needle.
